Overview

Schwab is a savings and loan holding company that sells wealth management, brokerage, banking, asset management, custody and advisory services. Scale at the 10-K date (FY2025): "At December 31, 2025, Schwab had $11.90 trillion in client assets, 38.5 million active brokerage accounts, 5.7 million workplace plan participant accounts, and 2.2 million banking accounts." [10-K.txt:L210] The business runs in two segments: "through two segments – Investor Services and Advisor Services" [10-K.txt:L221]. Scale at the Q3 2026 release (three months ended September 30, 2026): "with 40.3 million active brokerage accounts, 5.9 million workplace plan participant accounts, 2.4 million banking accounts, and $13.33 trillion in client assets" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L239].

Revenue model. "Schwab’s largest sources of net revenues are net interest revenue, asset management and administration fees, trading revenue, and bank deposit account fees." [10-K.txt:L318] FY2025 totals were "Total net revenues increased 22% year-over-year to $23.9 billion in 2025." and "Net interest revenue was $11.8 billion in 2025, up 28% from 2024" [10-K.txt:L1179]. The filings show three concentrations:
- Net interest revenue is the largest single stream, per the figure above.
- Counterparty concentration: "Under the 2023 IDA agreement, uninvested cash within eligible brokerage client accounts is swept off-balance sheet to deposit accounts at the TD Depository Institutions." [10-K.txt:L322]
- Fee concentration in a few fund categories: the funds "generated 50%, 49%, and 44% of the asset management and administration fees earned during 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively" [10-K.txt:L1977].

Management's growth thesis is a claim I test below: "currently exceeds $80 trillion, which means the Company’s $11.90 trillion in client assets leaves substantial opportunity for growth" [10-K.txt:L225]. The 10-K states the advantage as "creates a cost advantage that enables us to competitively price products and services" [10-K.txt:L233]. The filings give no market-share or peer data, so the size of the opportunity and the comparison with competitors are not established by the supplied evidence.

Market Positioning and Growth Outlook

Demand durability: SUPPORTED.
- Asset gathering (FY2025): "Core net new assets for 2025 totaled $519.4 billion, increasing 42% from the prior year, and resulting in an annualized organic growth rate of 5.1%." [10-K.txt:L1175]
- Account growth (FY2025): "active brokerage accounts totaled 38.5 million as of December 31, 2025, up 6% from year-end 2024" [10-K.txt:L1175].
- Q3 2026 asset gathering: "clients opened 1.2 million new brokerage accounts and entrusted Schwab with $190.4 billion in core net new assets – an annualized growth rate of 5.8%." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L22] Also "Core net new assets totaled $190.4 billion, up 38% versus 3Q25" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L56].
- Caveats on reported flows: the all-in figure was reduced by outflows, since "2025 includes net outflows of $20.8 billion from off-platform brokered CDs issued by CSB." [10-K.txt:L1162]
- Caveat on cash balances: part of the Q3 2026 cash growth is tied to a specific strategy: "Client transactional sweep cash balances ended September at $492.8 billion, an increase of $7.1 billion versus the prior quarter-end, reflecting continued demand for long/short strategies and organic growth, partially offset by client asset allocation decisions" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L197].
- Caveat on transient demand: trading volume is market-sensitive: "clients’ DATs were 7.7 million for full-year 2025 and 8.3 million in the fourth quarter, increasing 31% over both the prior year-to-date and fourth-quarter periods" [10-K.txt:L1175]. Q3 2026 read: "Daily average trading volume equaled 10.7 million – up 44% versus 3Q25" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L67].

Competitive position: MIXED.
- Supporting: both segments grew revenue at the same rate. "Total net revenues increased by 22% for both Investor Services and Advisor Services in 2025 compared to 2024." [10-K.txt:L2691] Expenses grew more slowly: "Investor Services and Advisor Services total expenses excluding interest increased by 5% and 4%, respectively, in 2025 compared to 2024." [10-K.txt:L2703] Profit followed: "Net income reached $8.9 billion in 2025, rising 49% from 2024, and diluted EPS was $4.65, an increase of 56% over the prior year." [10-K.txt:L1176] This is consistent with the claimed scale and cost advantage.
- Limiting: management ties the revenue gain to the funding mix more than to competitive wins. "Net interest revenue increased $2.6 billion, or 28%, in 2025 from 2024 primarily due to lower balances of bank supplemental funding, lower average rates paid on funding sources, growth in margin and bank lending" [10-K.txt:L1759].
- Limiting: the 10-K itself flags price pressure: "Increased price competition from other financial services firms to attract clients, such as reduced commissions, higher deposit rates, reduced mutual fund or ETF expense ratios, or the increased use of incentives, could impact our results of operations and financial condition." [10-K.txt:L519]
- Limiting: bank deposit account balances are shrinking even as fees rise. "This was partially offset by lower average BDA balances, which reduced the base on which bank deposit account fees are earned." [10-K.txt:L2233]
- Peer comparison and market share are not established by the supplied evidence.

Growth execution: MIXED.
- Organic lending growth is supported (FY2025): "margin loans ending the year at $112.3 billion, up 34% from year-end 2024" and "Bank loans totaled $58.0 billion at year-end 2025, increasing 28% during the year" [10-K.txt:L1188].
- Organic lending growth is supported (Q3 2026): "Margin loan balances increased 14% quarter-over-quarter to $187.9 billion at quarter-end, including $60.7 billion related to long/short strategies" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L64]. Also "Bank loan balances equaled $72.3 billion at September month-end, up 35% year-over-year" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L62].
- Revenue momentum continued: "Quarterly net revenues grew year-over-year by 17% to a record $7.2 billion" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L193], and "Asset management and administration fees grew by 14% year-over-year to $1.9 billion" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L201].
- Cost of expansion: FY2026 guidance in the 10-K is "We currently anticipate total expenses excluding interest in full-year 2026 will increase approximately 5.5% to 6.5% from 2025." [10-K.txt:L2368] Q3 2026 ran above that range: "GAAP expenses for the quarter increased 9% year-over-year" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L205]. Whether Forge costs explain the gap is not established by the supplied evidence, because the 10-K says Forge costs are excluded from guidance: "costs related to the operations and integration of Forge would be in addition to the 5.5% to 6.5% expected growth in expenses" [10-K.txt:L2368].
- Capital spending: "Capital expenditures were 2.5% of total net revenues in 2025, slightly lower than our previously disclosed expected range of approximately 3-5% of total net revenues." [10-K.txt:L2386] Q2 2026 included a large item: "Second quarter of 2026 includes incremental capital expenditures of $633 million related to a multi-year software license agreement with a corresponding liability recognized in long-term debt." [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L1014]
- Funding the lending growth: "To support growth in margin loan balances at our broker-dealer subsidiary while meeting our LCR requirements, the Company may utilize wholesale funding sources, such as issuing commercial paper, drawing on secured lines of credit" [10-K.txt:L2977].

Future Developments and Strategic Recommendations

Catalysts and developments to track:
- Forge: "in a transaction valued at approximately $660 million" and "is expected to close in March 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals." [10-K.txt:L244] The supplied release does not state whether it closed or what it contributed, so that is not established by the supplied evidence. The 10-K warns "we may not realize the anticipated benefits from an acquisition, including our acquisition of Forge, in a timely manner or at all" [10-K.txt:L509].
- Digital assets: "expanded access to select cryptocurrencies expected to be offered to clients beginning in 2026" [10-K.txt:L264]. The release says Schwab "plans to expand digital assets available in Schwab Crypto" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L71]. The risk factor cautions "Client demand for digital assets is uncertain and may fluctuate significantly due to market volatility, regulatory developments, or changes in investor sentiment." [10-K.txt:L512]
- AI tools: the release reports "Introduced Charley, a new AI-powered assistant that provides U.S. retail clients with conversational access to Schwab’s tools and insights" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L74]. No financial contribution is disclosed, so it is not established by the supplied evidence.
- Capital return: "Total common stock repurchased during the year amounted to $7.3 billion." [10-K.txt:L1193]

Recommendations for the analyst:
1. Treat asset gathering as the core demand test. Separate growth in long/short-related balances from organic cash growth, using the release's disclosure of "$60.7 billion related to long/short strategies" [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L64].
2. Do not credit the 2025 net interest revenue jump to competitive strength alone. Part of it came from funding-cost relief [10-K.txt:L1759].
3. Track whether expense growth returns toward the guided 5.5% to 6.5% range, and how much of any overage is Forge [10-K.txt:L2368].
4. Watch the dependence on TD-linked deposit fees given the shrinking BDA base [10-K.txt:L2233].

What would change my view: my strongest conclusion is that demand is durable. A next-filing (FY2026 10-K) annualized core net new asset organic growth rate below the 5.1% reported for 2025 [10-K.txt:L1175] would challenge it. It would show the 2025 gain, and the 5.8% quarterly rate in the Q3 2026 release [earnings_release_Ex99-1.txt:L22], was not sustained once market and trading tailwinds faded.

Insight: FY2025 net interest revenue growth of 28% leaned on a funding-cost lever that has largely been used, since bank supplemental funding was cut 90% to $5.1 billion, so further growth depends more on lending and asset gathering. [10-K.txt:L1188] "The Company reduced bank supplemental funding in 2025 by $44.8 billion, or 90%, to $5.1 billion at year-end 2025."
